next_guide.street_full_year: not found (stockanalysis forward P/E 41.4 at $685 implies ~$16.5 forward EPS, a derived figure, not a sourced estimate)
next_guide.company_current_guide: none formal; CFO on the 2026-08-11 call: 'revenue growth has accelerated, with approximately 14% growth in 2024, 15% growth in 2025, and mid-teen growth again this year' (https://www.elbitsystems.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/Q2_2026%20%20transcript%20.pdf)
next_guide.basis: Elbit does not guide; the only forward marker is the informal mid-teen 2026 growth remark and the CEO's 'you will continue to see growth in our backlog in the coming quarters', so a repeat of both is the likely outcome and the market will read Q4 order commentary (the $235m, $200m and $170m awards announced in Oct-Nov) instead of a guide.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue consensus of ~$2.28bn (Earnings Whispers; Benzinga snippet $2.35bn) implies +18.7-22% y/y on Q3 2025's $1.92bn and matches Q2's $2.287bn. The company's own marker is 'mid-teen growth again this year' (H1 grew 15.7%: $4,476m vs $3,869m), which puts Q3 nearer $2.21-2.23bn. Q2 was lifted by items management called one-time: Israel 37% of revenue 'following inventory replenishments on the back of the recent conflict with Iran', and Elbit of America +17% 'mainly due to a one-time favorable project mix', with the CEO adding growth 'may not continue at the exact pace seen this quarter'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue missed in Q3 2025 ($1.92bn vs $1.99bn) and the stock still rose ~5% on an EPS beat and record backlog; revenue beat in Q1 and Q2 2026 with reactions of +9% and -8%. Revenue alone has not decided the sign.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote the $2.28bn consensus and the backlog but none puts it next to the company's own mid-teen marker or the one-time labels on Q2. If this were priced, the consensus would sit near $2.21-2.23bn rather than at Q2's level. The bar itself is disputed between sources ($2.28bn vs $2.35bn), so this is capped small.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers also flags the Q2 one-offs fading (https://finviz.com/news/420403/elbits-record-32-billion-backlog-faces-a-conversion-test-as-shares-lag). Same transcript as finding 2's margin context, but a different line.

findings.finding: The EPS bar is soft. Consensus Q3 EPS $3.97 (whisper $4.08) is below Q2's actual non-GAAP $4.14. Elbit beat EPS by $0.62 (Q3'25), $0.54 (Q1'26) and $0.90 (Q2'26). Management said Q2's 10.4% non-GAAP operating margin 'surpassed our internal targets'. The 16.4% Pillar II tax rate is now a known drag rather than a surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS was beaten in each of the last three prints; reactions were +5%, +9% and -8%, so an EPS beat alone has not been rewarded reliably (Q2's $0.90 beat was sold 8%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: a beat is the base case for this name, and the whisper ($4.08) already sits above consensus. If an EPS beat were unpriced, the stock would not have fallen 8% on the largest beat in the series. Capped small because the bar is disputed (EW $3.97, Benzinga snippet $4.35, Barchart $3.44).
findings.independence: Q2 transcript (https://www.elbitsystems.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/Q2_2026%20%20transcript%20.pdf) on margins above internal targets; https://www.rttnews.com/3596145/elbit-systems-q3-profit-climbs-beats-market-but-revenues-miss.aspx for the Q3'25 beat.

findings.finding: Contract awards Elbit announced inside Q3 (Jul-Sep 2026) total about $0.65bn: CBP $370m (2026-07-20), an ISR payloads contract of about $270m (2026-09-01) and a $13.5m Navy radio deal. Awards announced in Q2 totalled about $2.7bn ($1.4bn European modernization, ~$750m Greece PULS, $350m tanks, ~$200m IMOD munitions), and backlog then rose $1.8bn to $32.0bn. Unless unannounced Israeli MoD orders were large, Q3 backlog growth is likely smaller than Q2's, on a stock whose reactions have followed the backlog headline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog headlines drove the last three reactions: +5% on record $25.2bn (Q3'25), +9% on >$30bn plus a $1.4bn award (Q1'26), -8% on $32.0bn (Q2'26, +$1.8bn q/q, a smaller step than Q1's).
findings.why_not_priced: No preview tallies the quarter's announced awards against Q2's; previews quote the $32bn figure as given. If this were priced, previews would carry a Q3 backlog estimate below or near $32bn. The counterweight is already in the size: many Israeli MoD orders are never press-released, and on 2026-08-11 the CEO said 'you will continue to see growth in our backlog in the coming quarters'. This is inference from announcements, not a reported backlog number.
findings.independence: Q2 awards are listed in the Q2 call transcript (https://www.elbitsystems.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/Q2_2026%20%20transcript%20.pdf). The $270m ISR award is at https://www.edrmagazine.eu/%E2%96%BA-elbit-systems-signed-contracts-with-an-international-customer-valued-at-approximately-270-million-for-advanced-isr-targeting-payloads (dated 2026-09-01 per https://www.calcalistech.com/tags/Elbit/1). The Navy radio award is at https://www.highergov.com/news/elbit-systems-wins-14-million-navy-survival-radio-6490031/.

findings.finding: Since the last call the company has announced Q4 awards of about $605m: ~$235m EXTRA-MR/PULS for a European country (2026-10-19), ~$200m airborne ISTAR/training in Asia-Pacific (2026-10-26) and a ~$170m, 15-year IDF artillery training centre (2026-11-02). It also announced a Swedish laser-warning production centre (2026-10-14). These give management fresh order momentum to cite on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Contract headlines have moved the stock on the day (e.g. +3.8% in Tel Aviv on the $370m CBP award, 2026-07-20, per Globes), but they fade, and award-day gains were partly given back in October.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because each was press-released and the stock rose on 10-26 (+5.8%). What is not priced is how management frames Q4 order intake on the call. Small.

findings.finding: Elbit's largest single customer, the Israeli Defense Ministry, owed Rafael, IAI and Elbit a record NIS 17bn (~$5.7bn) as of 2026-09-22, up from NIS 13-15.5bn earlier in the year. Elbit's share was put at about NIS 3bn (~$0.8-1.0bn) in an April report. Repayment depended on budget transfers scheduled for October and November, after Q3 closed. Israel was 37% of Q2 revenue, so Q3 operating cash flow and receivables may look worse than Q2's $237m operating cash flow and $150m FCF.
findings.link: The Israeli MoD is Elbit's customer for 37% of Q2 2026 revenue (Q2 call transcript); the debt is owed directly to Elbit among the three firms.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cash flow was cited in the March 2026 pullback after Q4'25 results (falling operating cash) and as a soft spot in Q2 coverage (FCF $150m vs $210m in Q1); not a line that has decided a print on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Reported in Israeli business press with no Elbit-specific Q3 figure; US previews do not mention it. If it were priced, previews would flag a Q3 working-capital build. The September article does not give Elbit's own portion (that is from an April report), so this is a counterparty proxy, sized small.
findings.independence: https://www.ynetnews.com/business/article/rjzqmg1abl (about April 2026; Elbit owed ~$800m) and https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/sjd1jznxmg (2026-07-02; budget deal to repay ~NIS 15bn, installments in October/November). Different documents, same underlying debt; counted once here.

The point is asymmetry: the same backlog headline that was sold from a high in August meets a stock already 10 points under its sector. If the market expected another sell-off, the skew would pay for puts; it pays for calls.

findings.link: Europe was 25% of Elbit's Q2 2026 revenue (Q2 transcript), and the Q2 backlog increase was 'mainly from Europe'. Both firms sell land systems, munitions and rocket artillery into European procurement, Elbit via EuroPULS with KNDS in Germany. No shared contract is named.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed for ESLT on a print day; ESLT fell -7.4% on 2026-11-05, the day of Rheinmetall's cut.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced via the Nov 5 move. What is unpriced is whether Elbit reports similar European timing slippage in revenue. Small, because Elbit's European revenue is mostly C4I and radios, with less ammunition exposure to German budget timing.

baseline_tension: The evidence is split. The lowered bar agrees with the upside-paid skew and the -10% relative run-up, while the revenue-bar and lighter-order findings cut against both. The net sits close to zero, consistent with a non-directional event-implied move of 6.1%.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (verify the bar): consensus sources disagree (EW $3.97/$2.28bn, Benzinga snippet $4.35/$2.35bn, Barchart $3.44), so the two bar-dependent findings were capped: revenue -0.6 to -0.4, EPS +0.6 to +0.3.

Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number) and rule 5 (inference is smaller than a document): the announced-orders backlog finding was cut from -1.2 to -0.8, because the CEO said backlog would keep growing and unannounced IMOD orders are common.
Rule 5 (proxy): the IMOD-debt finding was cut from -0.4 to -0.3, because the September article gives no Elbit-specific figure.

Rule 7 (positioning): short interest checked (0.5% of shares, DTC ~2.5), so no squeeze adjustment. The negatives run against an upside skew, which moved p_up from 48 to 49 rather than resizing findings again.

FPI history lesson: the baseline's 8-event history (median 1.27%) was flagged as monthly 6-K updates, so the base rate was rebuilt from three confirmed prints (+5%, +9%, -8%) and abs_move_pct kept at 7.0 against a 6.1% event-implied move.
Left standing: the expectations finding (+1.0), the peer and macro findings, and the next-guide zero.
